children: Indian shares opened lower on Wednesday, in line with global markets, as oil prices surged to a near-six-week high after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, intensifying the Middle East conflict and renewing concerns over inflation.
fell 0.82% to 23,858 and the BSE Sensex
shed 0.61% to 76,471.32 as of 9:15 a.m. IST.
All 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps

rose 1% to $95.4 a barrel, paring some gains after hitting a near-six-week-high earlier in the session, triggering a drop in Asian markets and lifting global bond yields on worries of a near-term U.S. rate hike.
Higher U.S. rates make emerging markets less attractive for global investors.
The U.S. said it had launched a series of airstrikes against targets in Iran overnight, prompting an Iranian response in a renewed escalation of tensions in the Middle East.

title: Indian shares open lower as widening Iran conflict sends oil higher
